observation.visible_scene: An indoor rug-cleaning bay with a white waterproof tarp covering the floor and a rectangular tan shaggy rug laid flat on the right. A worker wearing white rubber boots, dark trousers and black gloves holds a long-handled tool with a blue head and works along the left side of the tarp, where brown, dirty water pools and streaks. Wall-mounted cleaning tools (including 'PROTIME' squeegees) and a 'MOUNTAIN RUG CLEANING' logo are visible in the background. Midway through the excerpt the image cross-dissolves to a wider camera angle that reveals a back workbench with bottles, a blue floor blower and a wooden door.
visible_changes: Frames 1-16: the worker's gloved hands and the long-handled blue-headed tool shift back and forth along the left edge of the white tarp, pushing/working the dirty water line; the worker's boots stay roughly in place with small weight shifts.

Frames 17-26: an editing cross-dissolve blends the close, downward-tilted view with a wider, more level view; during the blend two overlapping images of the worker and the room are visible, indicating a cut/transition rather than continuous camera motion.

Frames 27-41 (post-transition): from the new wider angle the worker, now seen near the top of the frame, moves the blue squeegee head along the left trench/drain line, making small back-and-forth strokes; the brown water streak on the tarp remains largely static.
The tan shaggy rug on the right does not move or change shape throughout the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the worker does before the first frame and after the last frame (the segment is temporally cropped at both ends).
Whether water is being actively sprayed/added or only being squeegeed off; the source of the dirty water is not shown.
The exact function of the long-handled tool (squeegee vs. scrubbing wand) and any unseen operator or equipment behind the camera.
uncertain_details: The transition in the middle is an editing dissolve, so apparent 'motion' of the viewpoint is a cut between two camera setups, not a physical camera move.
Small positional differences of the worker's feet between the two camera angles cannot be reliably compared as continuous motion because the framing changes.
Whether the water line on the left is advancing or retreating is hard to confirm given the angle change.
